alt: Freeze-thaw in four stages: water enters a crack, freezes and expands, widens the crack and finally breaks a fragment off. Salt weathering forces rock apart as salt crystals grow in cracks; carbonation dissolves limestone and chalk with slightly acidic rainwater.
caption: Weathering breaks rock down in place and prepares cliffs for erosion.

alt: Three cliff cross-sections. Sliding: a block moves down a flat surface. Slumping: saturated clay rotates down a curved surface, leaving a curved scar. Rock fall: fragments break from a steep cliff, often one undercut by the sea, and fall to its foot.
caption: Sliding, slumping and rock falls are all movement of material downhill under gravity.

alt: Two plan views. On a discordant coast, hard and soft bands meet the sea at right angles: soft rock erodes into bays with beaches and hard rock stands out as headlands. On a concordant coast the bands run parallel to the shore; a resistant band protects softer rock until the sea breaks through and a rounded cove forms.
caption: The direction of the rock bands decides whether you get headlands and bays or coves.

alt: Three cross-sections. Waves cut a notch at the cliff base between high and low tide; the overhang above collapses and the cliff retreats; repeated over time, a gently sloping wave-cut platform is left at the foot of the cliff, exposed at low tide.
caption: Undercutting and collapse, repeated, move the cliff back and leave a platform.

alt: Two plan views of a bay. Longshore drift builds a spit part-way across it, with calm water behind. When the ridge reaches the land on the other side it becomes a bar, trapping a shallow lagoon.
caption: A bar is a spit that has closed off the bay, trapping a lagoon.
